content:
# Deuteronomy Chapter 11 — Disagreement Log
**Chapter:** Deuteronomy 11 (32 verses) | **Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA

---

## V.1 — Conjunction opening: "And you shall" vs. "You shall therefore" vs. imperative

- **EMET:** "And you shall love the LORD your God and you shall keep his charge and his statutes and his ordinances and his commandments all the days."
- **LOGOS:** "You shall therefore love the LORD your God and keep his charge, his statutes, his rules, and his commandments always."
- **PNEUMA:** "Love the LORD your God and keep his charge — his statutes, his ordinances, and his commands — always."
- **Rationale:** Three distinct issues: (1) the opening conjunction ve-; (2) "rules" vs. "ordinances" vs. "ordinances"; (3) "all the days" vs. "always" vs. "always." EMET preserves the Hebrew conjunctive chain literally. LOGOS uses "therefore" to signal logical connection to chapter 10. PNEUMA drops the conjunction entirely for a direct imperative. On "ordinances/rules": mishpatim = "ordinances" per project convention; LOGOS's "rules" departs from this. On "all the days" vs. "always": Hebrew kol ha-yamim = literally "all the days."
- **Ruling:** "You shall therefore love the LORD your God and keep his charge, his statutes, his ordinances, and his commandments all the days." — "Therefore" (LOGOS) is the appropriate logical connector from ch.10's doxology. "Ordinances" over "rules" per project convention. "All the days" (EMET) over "always" preserves the Hebrew literal form.
- **Status:** Resolved — LOGOS base with "ordinances" and "all the days."

---

## V.2 — Anacoluthon: "know" vs. "consider" / "sons" vs. "children" / structure of parenthetical

- **EMET:** "And you shall know today — for [I speak] not to your sons who did not know and who did not see the discipline of the LORD your God — his greatness, his strong hand and his outstretched arm,"
- **LOGOS:** "And consider today (since I am not speaking with your children who have not known and who have not seen the discipline of the LORD your God), his greatness, his mighty hand and his outstretched arm,"
- **PNEUMA:** "Know today — for it is not your children who are speaking with you; they have not seen and do not know — the discipline of the LORD your God: his greatness, his mighty hand, and his outstretched arm,"
- **Rationale:** Multiple divergences: (1) Hebrew yeda'atem = "you shall know" — LOGOS's "consider" is interpretively smoother but less literal; (2) "sons" vs. "children" — Hebrew beneikhem; (3) PNEUMA's "who are speaking with you" is an error — the text says Moses is speaking to adults who saw the exodus, not to their children; (4) "strong hand" vs. "mighty hand" — Hebrew yad chazaqah; (5) EMET's editorial "[I speak]" supplies the sense correctly.
- **Ruling:** "And you shall know today — for I am not speaking with your sons who have not known and who have not seen the discipline of the LORD your God — his greatness, his mighty hand and his outstretched arm," — Hebrew yada' = "know" retained. PNEUMA's "who are speaking with you" is erroneous; the parenthetical is Moses saying he is NOT addressing the next generation. "Sons" over "children" (Hebrew benim). "Mighty hand" (LOGOS/PNEUMA) over "strong hand" (EMET).
- **Status:** Resolved — EMET structure corrected with "mighty hand"; PNEUMA's mistaken rendering rejected.

---

## V.3 — "works" vs. "deeds" / "in the midst of Egypt" vs. "in Egypt" / "to Pharaoh" vs. "against Pharaoh"

- **EMET:** "and his signs and his works which he did in the midst of Egypt, to Pharaoh king of Egypt and to all his land,"
- **LOGOS:** "his signs and his deeds that he did in Egypt to Pharaoh the king of Egypt and to all his land,"
- **PNEUMA:** "his signs and the deeds he performed in the midst of Egypt, against Pharaoh king of Egypt and against all his land,"
- **Rationale:** (1) "works" vs. "deeds" — Hebrew ma'asav; (2) "in the midst of Egypt" vs. "in Egypt" — Hebrew betoch mitsrayim; (3) "to Pharaoh" vs. "against Pharaoh" — Hebrew be-Pharaoh; (4) "the king" vs. "king of Egypt" — article before title. Hebrew ma'asim can be "works" or "deeds." "In the midst of" preserves betoch. Hebrew be-Pharaoh most naturally reads "against Pharaoh" in context of plagues.
- **Ruling:** "and his signs and his works which he did in the midst of Egypt, against Pharaoh king of Egypt and against all his land," — "works" (EMET) is the more consistently used project rendering. "In the midst of" preserved. "Against Pharaoh" (PNEUMA) is contextually accurate for the plague narrative.
- **Status:** Resolved — EMET base with "against" from PNEUMA.

---

## V.4 — "overflow" vs. "flow over" vs. "swept" / "destroyed" tense / parenthetical structure

- **EMET:** "and what he did to the army of Egypt, to their horses and to their chariots, how he made the waters of the Red Sea [Yam Suph] overflow upon them as they pursued after you, and the LORD destroyed them unto this day,"
- **LOGOS:** "and what he did to the army of Egypt, to their horses and to their chariots, how he made the water of the Red Sea flow over them as they pursued after you, and how the LORD has destroyed them to this day,"
- **PNEUMA:** "and what he did to Egypt's army, to its horses and chariots — how he swept the waters of the Red Sea over them when they chased after you and the LORD destroyed them, and they have not recovered to this day —"
- **Rationale:** (1) "overflow upon them" vs. "flow over them" vs. "swept over them" — Hebrew tsippah aleihem; (2) "the LORD destroyed them unto/to this day" vs. "the LORD has destroyed them to this day" vs. "they have not recovered to this day" — PNEUMA adds "they have not recovered" which is not in the Hebrew; (3) "Red Sea" vs. "Red Sea" vs. "Red Sea" — all agree, though EMET adds [Yam Suph] gloss; (4) "army of Egypt" vs. "Egypt's army"; (5) "waters" (plural) vs. "water" (singular).
- **Ruling:** "and what he did to the army of Egypt, to their horses and to their chariots, how he made the waters of the Red Sea [Yam Suph] overflow upon them as they pursued after you, and the LORD destroyed them to this day," — "waters" (plural, EMET) reflects Hebrew ha-mayim. "Overflow upon them" over "swept" (too vivid) and "flow over" (too gentle). [Yam Suph] gloss retained per EMET convention. "To this day" (LOGOS over EMET's "unto"). PNEUMA's addition "they have not recovered" rejected as not in MT.
- **Status:** Resolved — EMET base with "to this day" from LOGOS; PNEUMA addition rejected.

---

## V.5 — "coming" vs. "came" vs. "arrived"

- **EMET:** "and what he did to you in the wilderness until your coming to this place,"
- **LOGOS:** "and what he did to you in the wilderness until you came to this place,"
- **PNEUMA:** "and what he did to you in the wilderness until you arrived at this place,"
- **Rationale:** Hebrew bo'akhem = "your coming" — a gerundive/nominal form. EMET preserves the noun form literally. LOGOS and PNEUMA convert to a finite verb clause. "Arrived at" (PNEUMA) vs. "came to" (LOGOS).
- **Ruling:** "and what he did to you in the wilderness until your coming to this place," — EMET's nominal form "your coming" preserves the Hebrew gerundive bo'akhem and is natural English. "Arrived at" (PNEUMA) is acceptable but "came to" or "coming to" is more standard.
- **Status:** Resolved — EMET retained.

---

## V.6 — "in their wake" vs. "that followed them" vs. "that belonged to them" / names transliteration

- **EMET:** "and what he did to Dathan and Aviram, sons of Eli'av son of Reuven, how the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them and their households and their tents and every living thing that was in their wake in the midst of all Yisra'el —"
- **LOGOS:** "and what he did to Dathan and Abiram the sons of Eliab, son of Reuben, how the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them up, with their households, their tents, and every living thing that followed them, in the midst of all Israel."
- **PNEUMA:** "and what he did to Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab son of Reuben — how the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them up along with their households, their tents, and every living thing that belonged to them, in the midst of all Israel."
- **Rationale:** (1) "Aviram" vs. "Abiram" — transliteration of Aviram; (2) "Eli'av" vs. "Eliab" — transliteration; (3) "Reuven" vs. "Reuben"; (4) "swallowed them" vs. "swallowed them up" — "up" not in Hebrew; (5) "in their wake" vs. "that followed them" vs. "that belonged to them" — Hebrew asher beragleihem = "at their feet/in their following"; (6) "Yisra'el" vs. "Israel."
- **Ruling:** "and what he did to Dathan and Abiram, sons of Eliab son of Reuben, how the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them and their households and their tents and every living thing that followed them, in the midst of all Israel." — English name forms per project convention (Abiram, Eliab, Reuben, Israel). "Swallowed them" without "up." "That followed them" (LOGOS) over "in their wake" (poetic) and "that belonged to them" (PNEUMA; too general — Hebrew asher beragleihem implies following).
- **Status:** Resolved — LOGOS base with English name forms.

---

## V.7 — "but your eyes" vs. "For your eyes" vs. "Your own eyes" / "great work" vs. "great works"

- **EMET:** "but your eyes — they saw every great work of the LORD which he did."
- **LOGOS:** "For your eyes have seen all the great work of the LORD that he did."
- **PNEUMA:** "Your own eyes have seen all the great works of the LORD that he has done."
- **Rationale:** (1) "but" vs. "For" vs. nothing — Hebrew ki = "for/because"; (2) "your eyes — they saw" (EMET emphatic construction) vs. "your eyes have seen" vs. "Your own eyes have seen"; (3) "great work" (singular) vs. "great works" (plural) — Hebrew kol-ha-ma'aseh ha-gadol = "every great work" (singular collective); (4) "which he did" vs. "that he did" vs. "that he has done."
- **Ruling:** "For your eyes have seen all the great work of the LORD that he did." — Hebrew ki = "for" (LOGOS). Singular "great work" (LOGOS/EMET) over "great works" (PNEUMA) follows the Hebrew collective singular. "Your eyes have seen" over EMET's inverted emphasis (which, though Hebrew, is awkward in English). PNEUMA's "has done" (present perfect) is less precise than simple past.
- **Status:** Resolved — LOGOS retained.

---

## V.8 — "every commandment" vs. "every commandment" / "go in and possess" vs. "go in and take possession of"

- **EMET:** "And you shall keep every commandment which I am commanding you today, in order that you may be strong and go in and possess the land into which you are crossing to possess it,"
- **LOGOS:** "You shall therefore keep every commandment that I command you today, that you may be strong, and go in and take possession of the land that you are going over to possess,"
- **PNEUMA:** "Therefore, keep every commandment I am giving you today, so that you will be strong enough to go in and take possession of the land you are crossing over to take,"
- **Rationale:** (1) "keep" vs. "keep" vs. "keep" — all agree; (2) "which I am commanding" vs. "that I command" vs. "I am giving" — PNEUMA's "giving" for tsavah (command) is too soft; (3) "in order that" vs. "that" vs. "so that"; (4) "possess" vs. "take possession of"; (5) "into which you are crossing to possess it" vs. "that you are going over to possess" vs. "you are crossing over to take."
- **Ruling:** "And you shall keep every commandment which I am commanding you today, in order that you may be strong and go in and take possession of the land into which you are crossing to possess it," — EMET's "which I am commanding" preserves the present participial force. "In order that" (EMET) is more formal/accurate. "Take possession of" (LOGOS/PNEUMA) is the established rendering for yarash. "Into which you are crossing" (EMET) over "going over."
- **Status:** Resolved — EMET base with "take possession of" from LOGOS.

---

## V.9 — "lengthen your days" vs. "live long" / "seed" vs. "offspring" vs. "descendants"

- **EMET:** "and in order that you may lengthen your days upon the ground which the LORD swore to your fathers to give to them and to their seed — a land flowing with milk and honey."
- **LOGOS:** "and that you may live long in the land that the LORD swore to your fathers to give to them and to their offspring, a land flowing with milk and honey."
- **PNEUMA:** "and so that you will live long in the land the LORD swore to give to your ancestors and their descendants — a land flowing with milk and honey."
- **Rationale:** (1) "lengthen your days" vs. "live long" — Hebrew lema'an ya'arikhu yameikhem = literally "in order that your days may be prolonged/lengthened"; (2) "upon the ground" vs. "in the land" — Hebrew al ha-adamah; (3) "seed" vs. "offspring" vs. "descendants" — Hebrew zar'am; (4) "your fathers" vs. "your ancestors."
- **Ruling:** "and in order that you may lengthen your days upon the ground which the LORD swore to your fathers to give to them and to their seed — a land flowing with milk and honey." — "Lengthen your days" (EMET) preserves the Hebrew idiom ya'arikhu yameikhem. "Upon the ground" preserves adamah. "Fathers" over "ancestors" (project convention for avot). "Seed" (EMET) over "offspring/descendants" per project convention.
- **Status:** Resolved — EMET retained.

---

## V.10 — "garden of vegetables" vs. "garden of vegetables" / "where you came out" vs. "from which you came out"

- **EMET:** "For the land into which you are going in to possess it — it is not like the land of Egypt from which you came out, where you sowed your seed and watered [it] with your foot like a garden of vegetables."
- **LOGOS:** "For the land that you are entering to take possession of it is not like the land of Egypt, from which you came out, where you sowed your seed and watered it with your foot, like a garden of vegetables."
- **PNEUMA:** "The land you are entering to take possession of is not like the land of Egypt, where you came from — where you sowed your seed and watered it with your foot like a vegetable garden."
- **Rationale:** (1) "going in to possess it" vs. "entering to take possession of it"; (2) EMET's "it is not" includes an emphatic pronoun (hi einenah); (3) "from which you came out" vs. "where you came from" — relative clause construction; (4) "garden of vegetables" vs. "vegetable garden" — Hebrew gan ha-yareq.
- **Ruling:** "For the land into which you are going in to possess it — it is not like the land of Egypt from which you came out, where you sowed your seed and watered it with your foot like a garden of vegetables." — EMET's dash construction preserves the Hebrew topic-comment structure (topicalization with pronoun resumption). "From which you came out" over PNEUMA's "where you came from." "Garden of vegetables" preserves the Hebrew word order.
- **Status:** Resolved — EMET base with "it" added for "watered it."

---

## V.11 — "hills and valleys" vs. "hills and valleys" / "mountains and valleys" / "rain of the heavens" vs. "rain from heaven"

- **EMET:** "But the land into which you are crossing to possess it — a land of hills and valleys, by the rain of the heavens it drinks water —"
- **LOGOS:** "But the land that you are going over to possess is a land of hills and valleys, which drinks water by the rain from heaven,"
- **PNEUMA:** "But the land you are crossing over to possess is a land of mountains and valleys that drinks in water from the rain of the sky —"
- **Rationale:** (1) "hills and valleys" vs. "mountains and valleys" — Hebrew harim u-veqa'ot; harim = mountains, but often rendered "hills" in Deuteronomy; (2) "rain of the heavens" vs. "rain from heaven" vs. "rain of the sky" — Hebrew geshem ha-shamayim; (3) "sky" (PNEUMA) vs. "heaven/heavens."
- **Ruling:** "But the land into which you are crossing to possess it — a land of hills and valleys, which drinks water by the rain of the heavens —" — Hebrew harim can be "mountains" or "hills"; Deuteronomy's Canaan is described in terms of "hills" more naturally in context (EMET/LOGOS). "Of the heavens" (EMET) preserves the genitive of shamayim. "Sky" (PNEUMA) is too colloquial here.
- **Status:** Resolved — EMET base with "which drinks water" from LOGOS.

---

## V.12 — "seeks" vs. "cares for" / "always" vs. "continually" / end of year

- **EMET:** "a land which the LORD your God seeks; the eyes of the LORD your God are always upon it, from the beginning of the year and unto the end of the year."
- **LOGOS:** "a land that the LORD your God cares for. The eyes of the LORD your God are on it continually, from the beginning of the year to the end of the year."
- **PNEUMA:** "a land the LORD your God cares for. The eyes of the LORD your God are always on it, from the beginning of the year to the year's end."
- **Rationale:** (1) "seeks" vs. "cares for" — Hebrew doresh = to seek, inquire after, care for; (2) "always" vs. "continually" — Hebrew tamid; (3) "unto the end of the year" vs. "to the end of the year" vs. "to the year's end."
- **Ruling:** "a land that the LORD your God cares for. The eyes of the LORD your God are on it continually, from the beginning of the year to the end of the year." — Hebrew doresh in this context means "seeks/cares for" — LOGOS/PNEUMA's "cares for" captures the relational sense better than EMET's "seeks" (which implies the land is absent). "Continually" for tamid (LOGOS) is more precise than "always." "To the end of the year" (LOGOS) over EMET's archaic "unto."
- **Status:** Resolved — LOGOS retained.

---

## V.13 — "if you indeed hearken" vs. "if you will indeed obey" vs. "if you will indeed listen" / "all your soul" vs. "all your life"

- **EMET:** "And it shall be, if you indeed hearken to my commandments which I am commanding you today, to love the LORD your God and to serve him with all your heart and with all your soul —"
- **LOGOS:** "And if you will indeed obey my commandments that I command you today, to love the LORD your God, and to serve him with all your heart and with all your soul,"
- **PNEUMA:** "If you will indeed listen to my commands that I am giving you today — to love the LORD your God and to serve him with all your heart and all your life —"
- **Rationale:** (1) "hearken" vs. "obey" vs. "listen" — Hebrew shamo'a tishme'u = literally "hearing you shall hear" (infinitive absolute); (2) "And it shall be" vs. nothing — Hebrew ve-hayah; (3) "commandments" vs. "commands" — Hebrew mitsvotai; (4) "all your soul" vs. "all your life" — Hebrew kol nafshekhem; Shema convention.
- **Ruling:** "And it shall be, if you indeed hearken to my commandments which I am commanding you today, to love the LORD your God and to serve him with all your heart and with all your soul —" — "And it shall be" preserves ve-hayah. "Hearken" (EMET) over "obey" (LOGOS) or "listen" (PNEUMA) for shama, which means "to hear/heed." Infinitive absolute "indeed hearken" captures the Hebrew emphasis. "All your soul" per Shema convention (cf. DEU_010 ruling on 10:12).
- **Status:** Resolved — EMET retained.

---

## V.14 — "then I will give" vs. "he will give" / "early rain and the latter rain" vs. "early rain and the later rain" / bracketed terms

- **EMET:** "then I will give the rain of your land in its season, the early rain and the latter rain [yoreh u-malqosh], and you shall gather your grain and your new wine and your fresh oil,"
- **LOGOS:** "he will give the rain of your land in its season, the early rain and the later rain, that you may gather in your grain and your wine and your oil."
- **PNEUMA:** "then I will send rain on your land in its season, both the early rains and the late rains, and you will gather in your grain, your new wine, and your olive oil."
- **Rationale:** (1) "I will give" vs. "he will give" — this is a known MT textual point; the change from second person Moses to third person refers to God; MT has first person "I will give" — God speaking through Moses; (2) "the rain of your land" vs. "rain on your land" — Hebrew geshem artsekhem; (3) "latter rain" vs. "later rain" vs. "late rains" — malqosh; (4) "your new wine" vs. "your wine" — Hebrew tiroshekha; (5) "your fresh oil" vs. "your oil" vs. "your olive oil" — Hebrew yitsharekha; (6) PNEUMA's "send" for natan (give).
- **Ruling:** "then I will give the rain of your land in its season, the early rain and the latter rain [yoreh u-malqosh], and you shall gather your grain and your new wine and your fresh oil," — "I will give" follows the MT first-person construction. "Give" (EMET/LOGOS) over "send" (PNEUMA) for natan. "Latter rain" is the traditional English term for malqosh; "later rain" (LOGOS) is acceptable but "latter rain" has established agricultural and liturgical usage. [yoreh u-malqosh] gloss retained. "New wine" and "fresh oil" (EMET) over LOGOS's "wine" and "oil" — Hebrew tiyrosh and yitshar are specifically new/fresh harvest products, not aged wine and oil.
- **Status:** Resolved — EMET retained.

---

## V.15 — "grass" / "be satisfied" vs. "be full"

- **EMET:** "and I will give grass in your fields for your livestock, and you shall eat and be satisfied."
- **LOGOS:** "And he will give grass in your fields for your livestock, and you shall eat and be full."
- **PNEUMA:** "I will provide grass in your fields for your livestock, and you will eat and be satisfied."
- **Rationale:** (1) "I will give" vs. "he will give" — same person-shift issue as v.14; (2) "give" vs. "provide" — Hebrew natan; (3) "be satisfied" vs. "be full" — Hebrew sevata = to be sated/satisfied/full.
- **Ruling:** "and I will give grass in your fields for your livestock, and you shall eat and be satisfied." — "I will give" consistent with v.14. "Give" over "provide." "Satisfied" (EMET/PNEUMA) over "full" (LOGOS) — sava = satiety/satisfaction, more than mere fullness.
- **Status:** Resolved — EMET retained.

---

## V.16 — "Be careful lest" vs. "Take care lest" vs. "Watch yourselves" / "deceived" vs. "seduced" / "turn and serve" vs. "turn aside and serve"

- **EMET:** "Be careful lest your heart be deceived and you turn and serve other gods and bow down to them,"
- **LOGOS:** "Take care lest your heart be deceived, and you turn aside and serve other gods and bow down to them;"
- **PNEUMA:** "Watch yourselves — do not let your hearts be seduced, so that you turn aside and serve other gods and bow down to them."
- **Rationale:** (1) "Be careful" vs. "Take care" vs. "Watch yourselves" — Hebrew hishhameru lakhem; (2) "your heart" (singular) vs. "your hearts" (plural) — Hebrew levavkhem; (3) "deceived" vs. "deceived" vs. "seduced" — Hebrew yifteh = to be open/enticed; (4) "turn and serve" vs. "turn aside and serve" — Hebrew ve-sartem = "and you turn/turn aside"; (5) singular/plural "heart."
- **Ruling:** "Take care lest your heart be deceived and you turn aside and serve other gods and bow down to them," — "Take care" (LOGOS) is slightly more natural than "Be careful" for hishhameru. "Your heart" singular per Hebrew levavkhem (collective singular). "Deceived" (EMET/LOGOS) over "seduced" (PNEUMA) — PNEUMA's note on the erotic sense is interesting but "deceived" better captures the simple warning register. "Turn aside" (LOGOS/PNEUMA) over "turn" alone.
- **Status:** Resolved — LOGOS retained.

---

## V.17 — "burn against you" vs. "be kindled against you" / "shut up the heavens" vs. "shut up the sky" / "not yield its produce" vs. "yield no fruit"

- **EMET:** "and the anger of the LORD burn against you and he shut up the heavens and there be no rain, and the ground not yield its produce, and you perish quickly from upon the good land which the LORD is giving you."
- **LOGOS:** "then the anger of the LORD will be kindled against you, and he will shut up the heavens, so that there will be no rain, and the land will yield no fruit, and you will perish quickly off the good land that the LORD is giving you."
- **PNEUMA:** "Then the LORD's anger will burn against you, and he will shut up the sky so that there will be no rain. The ground will not yield its fruit, and you will perish quickly from the good land the LORD is giving you."
- **Rationale:** (1) "burn" vs. "be kindled" — Hebrew ve-charah = "and it will burn/blaze"; (2) "the heavens" vs. "the sky" — Hebrew ha-shamayim; (3) "the ground not yield its produce" vs. "the land will yield no fruit" vs. "The ground will not yield its fruit" — Hebrew ve-ha-adamah lo titein et yevulah; (4) "from upon" vs. "off" vs. "from."
- **Ruling:** "and the anger of the LORD burn against you and he shut up the heavens and there be no rain, and the ground not yield its produce, and you perish quickly from upon the good land which the LORD is giving you." — "Burn" (EMET/PNEUMA) over "be kindled" for charah — "burn" is more direct. "The heavens" (EMET/LOGOS) over "the sky" (PNEUMA). "The ground" (EMET) preserves adamah. "Its produce" (EMET) over "fruit" — Hebrew yevulah = produce/yield. "From upon" (EMET) preserves the Hebrew me'al idiom.
- **Status:** Resolved — EMET retained.

---

## V.18 — "put upon" vs. "lay up" vs. "fix on" / "totafot" preserved vs. "frontlets" / "upon your soul" vs. "in your soul"

- **EMET:** "And you shall put these my words upon your heart and upon your soul, and you shall bind them as a sign upon your hand, and they shall be for frontlets [totafot] between your eyes."
- **LOGOS:** "You shall therefore lay up these words of mine in your heart and in your soul, and you shall bind them as a sign on your hand, and they shall be as frontlets between your eyes."
- **PNEUMA:** "Fix these words of mine on your hearts and in your lives. Tie them as a sign on your hands and let them serve as a mark between your eyes."
- **Rationale:** (1) "put" vs. "lay up" vs. "Fix" — Hebrew ve-samtem = "and you shall place/put"; (2) "upon your heart and upon your soul" vs. "in your heart and in your soul" — Hebrew al levavkhem ve-al nafshekhem; (3) "frontlets [totafot]" vs. "frontlets" vs. "a mark" — Hebrew totafot; (4) "your soul" vs. "your lives" — Hebrew nafshekhem; (5) "bind" vs. "bind" vs. "Tie" — Hebrew ukshartem.
- **Ruling:** "And you shall put these my words upon your heart and upon your soul, and you shall bind them as a sign upon your hand, and they shall be for frontlets [totafot] between your eyes." — "Put" (EMET) for samtem. "Upon your heart and upon your soul" preserves the Hebrew al preposition. "Frontlets [totafot]" (EMET) — the traditional term with the Hebrew preserved in brackets per project convention. PNEUMA's "a mark" loses the technical term. "Your soul" over "your lives" per nefesh convention.
- **Status:** Resolved — EMET retained.

---

## V.19 — "teach them to your sons" vs. "teach them to your children" / "speaking of them" vs. "talking of them"

- **EMET:** "And you shall teach them to your sons, speaking of them when you sit in your house and when you walk on the road and when you lie down and when you rise up."
- **LOGOS:** "You shall teach them to your children, talking of them when you are sitting in your house, and when you are walking by the way, and when you lie down, and when you rise."
- **PNEUMA:** "Teach them to your children, speaking about them when you sit at home and when you walk along the road, when you lie down and when you get up."
- **Rationale:** (1) "sons" vs. "children" — Hebrew beneikhem; (2) "speaking of them" vs. "talking of them" vs. "speaking about them" — Hebrew ve-dibbarta bam; (3) "in your house" vs. "at home"; (4) "on the road" vs. "by the way" vs. "along the road" — Hebrew ba-derekh; (5) "rise up" vs. "rise" vs. "get up."
- **Ruling:** "And you shall teach them to your sons, speaking of them when you sit in your house and when you walk on the road and when you lie down and when you rise up." — "Sons" (EMET) per project convention for benim. "Speaking of them" (EMET) = ve-dibbarta bam more precisely than "about them." "In your house" and "on the road" preserved. "Rise up" (EMET) is more literal; "rise" (LOGOS) and "get up" (PNEUMA) are also acceptable but "rise up" is more dignified.
- **Status:** Resolved — EMET retained.

## V.21 — "days of the heavens over the earth" vs. "as long as the heavens are above the earth" / "sons" vs. "children"

- **EMET:** "in order that your days and the days of your sons may multiply upon the ground which the LORD swore to your fathers to give them — like the days of the heavens over the earth."
- **LOGOS:** "that your days and the days of your children may be multiplied in the land that the LORD swore to your fathers to give them, as long as the heavens are above the earth."
- **PNEUMA:** "so that as long as the sky remains over the earth, your days and your children's days may be multiplied in the land the LORD swore to give your ancestors."
- **Rationale:** (1) "sons" vs. "children" — Hebrew beneikhem; (2) "multiply upon the ground" vs. "be multiplied in the land" — Hebrew yirbu al ha-adamah; (3) "like the days of the heavens over the earth" vs. "as long as the heavens are above the earth" — Hebrew ki-mei ha-shamayim al ha-aretz; (4) PNEUMA's "sky" for shamayim; (5) "your fathers" vs. "your ancestors."
- **Ruling:** "in order that your days and the days of your sons may multiply upon the ground which the LORD swore to your fathers to give them — like the days of the heavens over the earth." — "Sons" per convention. "Multiply upon the ground" preserves adamah and the active verb. "Like the days of the heavens over the earth" (EMET) is the most literal rendering of ki-mei ha-shamayim al ha-aretz — a beautiful simile comparing longevity to the timelessness of sky over earth. LOGOS's "as long as" converts the simile to a temporal clause; PNEUMA's "sky" is too colloquial.
- **Status:** Resolved — EMET retained.

## V.22 — "carefully keep" vs. "be careful to do" / "cling" vs. "holding fast" vs. "clinging"

- **EMET:** "For if you carefully keep all this commandment which I am commanding you to do it — to love the LORD your God, to walk in all his ways and to cling to him —"
- **LOGOS:** "For if you will be careful to do all this commandment that I command you to do, loving the LORD your God, walking in all his ways, and holding fast to him,"
- **PNEUMA:** "If you carefully keep all these commands I am giving you to follow — loving the LORD your God, walking in all his ways, and clinging to him —"
- **Rationale:** (1) "carefully keep" vs. "be careful to do" — Hebrew tishmeru laasoht; (2) "all this commandment" (singular) vs. "all these commands" (PNEUMA plural) — Hebrew et kol ha-mitsvah ha-zot (singular); (3) "to cling to him" vs. "holding fast to him" vs. "clinging to him" — Hebrew u-ledovqah vo; (4) "I am commanding you to do it" vs. "I command you to do" — Hebrew particle; (5) infinitival vs. participial construction for the three actions.
- **Ruling:** "For if you carefully keep all this commandment which I am commanding you to do — to love the LORD your God, to walk in all his ways, and to cling to him —" — "Carefully keep" (EMET) over "be careful to do" — the Hebrew shamerim laasoht is better captured this way. "All this commandment" (singular, EMET/LOGOS) per the Hebrew. "To cling to him" (EMET) preserves the infinitive form and uses "cling" for dabaq per project convention (cf. DEU_010 v.20 ruling).
- **Status:** Resolved — EMET base with slight smoothing of "to do it."

## V.23 — "drive out" / "dispossess" vs. "possess greater and mightier" / nations comparison

- **EMET:** "then the LORD will drive out all these nations from before you and you shall possess greater and mightier nations than you."
- **LOGOS:** "then the LORD will drive out all these nations before you, and you will dispossess nations greater and mightier than you."
- **PNEUMA:** "then the LORD will drive out all these nations before you and you will dispossess nations greater and more powerful than you."
- **Rationale:** (1) "from before you" vs. "before you" — Hebrew mi-lefneikhem; (2) "possess" vs. "dispossess" — Hebrew veyareshtem = "and you shall possess/dispossess" (yarash can mean both to possess and to dispossess/drive out); (3) "mightier" vs. "more powerful" — Hebrew ve-atsumim = and mighty/numerous.
- **Ruling:** "then the LORD will drive out all these nations from before you and you shall dispossess nations greater and mightier than you." — "From before you" (EMET) preserves mi-lefneikhem. "Dispossess" (LOGOS/PNEUMA) is the more precise rendering of yarash here — the nations are being dispossessed, not simply possessed. "Mightier" (EMET/LOGOS) over "more powerful" (PNEUMA) for atsumim.
- **Status:** Resolved — EMET base with "dispossess" from LOGOS.

## V.24 — "western sea" vs. "western sea" vs. "Western Sea" / "ha-yam ha-acharon" gloss / territory description structure

- **EMET:** "Every place where the sole of your foot treads shall be yours — from the wilderness and the Levanon, from the river, the Euphrates River, and unto the western sea [ha-yam ha-acharon] shall be your territory."

- **Ruling:** "Every place where the sole of your foot treads shall be yours — from the wilderness to Lebanon and from the River, the Euphrates River, to the western sea [ha-yam ha-acharon] shall be your territory." — "Lebanon" (standard English). "The River, the Euphrates River" follows the Hebrew appositive construction ha-nahar nahar perat. [ha-yam ha-acharon] gloss retained per EMET convention. "Western sea" lowercase per standard. "To Lebanon" (LOGOS/PNEUMA) over EMET's "and the Lebanon."

## V.25 — "dread...and fear" vs. "fear...and dread" word order / "put upon" vs. "lay upon" vs. "spread"

- **EMET:** "No man shall stand before you; the LORD your God will put the dread of you and the fear of you upon all the face of the ground that you shall tread, as he spoke to you."
- **LOGOS:** "No one shall be able to stand against you. The LORD your God will lay the fear of you and the dread of you on all the land that you tread, as he promised you."
- **PNEUMA:** "No one will be able to stand against you. The LORD your God will spread the fear and dread of you over all the land you tread on, just as he has promised you."
- **Rationale:** (1) "No man" vs. "No one" — Hebrew lo yityatsev ish; (2) "before you" vs. "against you" — Hebrew bifneikhem; (3) "put" vs. "lay" vs. "spread" — Hebrew yiten = will give/put; (4) "dread...and fear" vs. "fear...and dread" vs. combined — Hebrew et pachdekhem ve-et mor'akhem; (5) "face of the ground" vs. "land" — Hebrew al penei kol ha-aretz; (6) "as he spoke to you" vs. "as he promised you" — Hebrew ka'asher dibber aleikhem.
- **Ruling:** "No man shall stand before you; the LORD your God will put the dread of you and the fear of you upon all the face of the ground that you shall tread, as he spoke to you." — "No man" (EMET) preserves ish. "Before you" (EMET) for bifneikhem. "Put" (EMET) for yiten. Hebrew has pachdekhem first, then mor'akhem — "dread" then "fear" (EMET). "Face of the ground" (EMET) preserves penei ha-aretz. "As he spoke to you" over "promised" — dibber = spoke.
- **Status:** Resolved — EMET retained.

## V.29 — "give the blessing upon" vs. "set the blessing on" vs. "proclaim the blessing on" / mountain names

- **LOGOS:** "And when the LORD your God brings you into the land that you are entering to take possession of it, you shall set the blessing on Mount Gerizim and the curse on Mount Ebal."
- **PNEUMA:** "When the LORD your God brings you into the land you are going in to take possession of, you are to proclaim the blessing on Mount Gerizim and the curse on Mount Ebal."
- **Rationale:** (1) "give the blessing" vs. "set the blessing" vs. "proclaim the blessing" — Hebrew natatah et ha-berakha; (2) "upon" vs. "on"; (3) "Eival" vs. "Ebal" — transliteration of Har Eyval; (4) "And it shall be" vs. nothing — Hebrew ve-hayah; (5) EMET's [Har Gerizim] and [Har Eival] glosses.

## V.30 — "behind the road" vs. "west of the road" / "oaks of Moreh" vs. "oak of Moreh" / geographic terms

- **EMET:** "Are they not across the Yarden, behind the road of the going-down of the sun, in the land of the Canaanite dwelling in the Aravah, opposite Gilgal, beside the oaks [elonei] of Moreh?"
- **LOGOS:** "Are they not beyond the Jordan, west of the road, toward the going down of the sun, in the land of the Canaanites who live in the Arabah, opposite Gilgal, beside the oak of Moreh?"
- **PNEUMA:** "Are they not beyond the Jordan, past the road to the west, in the land of the Canaanites who live in the Arabah, opposite Gilgal, near the oak of Moreh?"
- **Rationale:** (1) "Yarden" vs. "Jordan" — transliteration; (2) "across" vs. "beyond" — Hebrew me'ever = across/beyond; (3) "behind the road of the going-down of the sun" vs. "west of the road" vs. "past the road to the west" — Hebrew acharei derekh mevo ha-shemesh; (4) "the Canaanite" (singular collective) vs. "the Canaanites" — Hebrew ha-kena'ani; (5) "the Aravah" vs. "the Arabah" — Hebrew ha-aravah; (6) "oaks [elonei] of Moreh" vs. "oak of Moreh" — Hebrew elonei = plural of elon; (7) "opposite" vs. "opposite" vs. "opposite."
- **Ruling:** "Are they not beyond the Jordan, behind the road toward the going-down of the sun, in the land of the Canaanite dwelling in the Arabah, opposite Gilgal, beside the oaks [elonei] of Moreh?" — "Jordan" (standard English). "Beyond" for me'ever. "Behind the road toward the going-down of the sun" — a compressed rendering of derekh mevo ha-shemesh; LOGOS's "west of the road" is clear but loses the Hebrew idiom; EMET's "behind the road of the going-down of the sun" is more literal. "The Canaanite" (singular collective, EMET). "The Arabah" (LOGOS/PNEUMA standard English) over "Aravah" (EMET). "Oaks [elonei] of Moreh" (EMET) — the Hebrew has the plural form; LOGOS/PNEUMA's singular "oak" flattens this.
- **Status:** Resolved — EMET base with "Jordan" and "Arabah."

## V.31 — "For you are crossing over" vs. "For you are to cross over" / "dwell in it" vs. "live in it" vs. "settled in it"

"Dwell in it" (EMET) over "live in it" (LOGOS) and "settled in it" (PNEUMA past tense) — Hebrew veyashavtem = shall dwell. The verse is one continuous sentence (EMET structure).
